This binder belongs to the theorem itself. Nothing else in the statement mentions it: `Hom.ker`, `vanishingIdeal`, `Closeds.closure` and `Set.range` need no quasi-compactness to elaborate. The only place it is used is the helper `Scheme.Hom.ker_eq_vanishingIdeal_closure_range`, through `f.ker_radical_of_isReduced_source` (which relies on `Hom.ker_apply` and needs `[QuasiCompact f]`) and `support_ker`.

For a reduced source, the per-morphism equality holds for every morphism; this is Stacks 01R8. It can be proved from Mathlib as follows.

(≤) `Hom.range_subset_ker_support` (Basic.lean:757) has no quasi-compactness assumption. Since the support is closed, `closure (range f) ≤ f.ker.support`. By `le_support_iff_le_vanishingIdeal`, `f.ker ≤ vanishingIdeal (closure (range f))`.

(≥) `Hom.ker` is defined as `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`. By `le_ofIdeals_iff`, it is enough to show `vanishingIdeal Z`.ideal U ⊆ ker (f.app U) for each affine open U. That ideal is `PrimeSpectrum.vanishingIdeal (U.fromSpec ⁻¹' Z)`. Take s in it. Then `Y.basicOpen s` does not meet Z ∩ U, and Z contains `range f`. Hence `X.basicOpen (f.app U s) = f ⁻¹ᵁ Y.basicOpen s = ⊥`, and `eq_zero_of_basicOpen_eq_bot` (Properties.lean:178, which needs only `[IsReduced X]` and works for any open) gives `f.app U s = 0`.

With this equality in hand, the rest of the proof (`vanishingIdeal_iSup`, `congr`, `funext`) goes through unchanged. Deleting the binder is a pure deletion, and the statement stays true and provable.
